name: issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_ceiling_breach
description: Symmetric companion to issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_floor_breach.json: a cool day (native heating), recency window cleared, indoor rises above comfort_cool -- the switch to cool must land within one sustain-confirm window of the reactive temperature tick, without a second explicit classification cycle.
notes: The user explicitly asked for this to be symmetric: the same reactive-tick guarantee that
closes the heat-side incident must also apply to a ceiling breach on a cool-classified day.
comfort_family_temperature_check()'s gate is direction-agnostic (checks current_temp against
both band.floor and band.ceiling), and comfort_family_decision.py's
_against_grain_deadband() is already symmetric by construction -- this scenario proves the
reactive wiring inherits that symmetry rather than only having been exercised heat-side.
check (`current_temp > band.ceiling`) makes this scenario fail identically to how
reverting the floor-side check fails the companion scenario.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: same automation logic table row as the floor-side scenario,
(c) Occupant experience: a home drifting above the comfort ceiling on a cool day (e.g. an
unseasonably warm afternoon) gets cooling engaged within about a minute and a half of the
drift being detected, not up to 30 minutes later.

events.note: Cool-day classification (native heating). Only classification event in this scenario.

First breach tick: 1F above comfort_cool(72), unseasonably warm afternoon. Cold-start engine -- nothing recorded as recently heating, so the recency-gated deadband is already 0F. comfort_family_temperature_check() fires reactively (indoor > band.ceiling); sustain-confirm candidate starts here.
120s after the first breach tick (>90s sustain window). Reactive check fires again, sustain-confirms, escalates to cooling -- with no second classification event ever having run.

assertions.reason: Baseline: cool day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally at the floor.
Issue #858: the switch to cooling lands by 14:02 -- 2 minutes after the first breach tick -- driven entirely by the reactive temperature-tick path, symmetric with the heat-side companion scenario.
Final engine state confirms the family actually escalated, not just an emitted event.
The escalated mode is a real climate.set_temperature/set_hvac_mode call at comfort_cool, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A ceiling breach resolves to cool within one sustain-confirm window of the reactive temperature tick, symmetric with the heat-side fix (Issue #858).
verdict.observed_behavior: Single classification event at 06:00 (cool/heat), indoor rises above the ceiling via temp_update alone at 14:00 and 14:02 -- comfort family escalates to cooling by 14:02, driven entirely by the reactive tick.
verdict.expected_behavior: The reactive comfort-family re-evaluation must be direction-agnostic -- a ceiling breach on a cool day gets the same fast-detection guarantee as a floor breach on a warm day.
